title: Bound GL3 order-seven sharing with one dirty register
body:
## Exact scoped result

In the formal algebra `F2[GL3(F2)]`, the target `diag([C],[C],1)` with `C=C01*C12*C20` has exact minimum six paid coordinate-CNOT calls on three scalar registers, even with free scalar `GL3(F2)` mixing and one arbitrary dirty register. The six-call direct word is checked on all 504 regular-action basis rows.

The verifier exhausts the 22,051-state identity ball through radius two and streams all 4,770,025 target-side words through radius three. There are zero intersections, excluding every word through five calls. All 168 factors, their inverses, and positive/negative controls are checked.

## Scope and limitations

This is a finite model result for one order-seven target and exactly three scalar registers. It identifies no multiplication supplier, recursive-moment saving, new `kappa`, physical compiler/hosting cost, precision interface, or full multiplication theorem. The selected record and inherited assumptions are unchanged.

Reproduce from the repository root with Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/gl3-order7-dirty-register-seed39ae
```

## Assignment and overlap

Seed `39ae4eb03387f147b3cd06da8e84b83e`, track `bit-mechanisms`, task `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 3. Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

PR #1567 covers two-register GL3 target pairs with full six-label coordinate-CNOT alphabet and direct cost at most nine; this package adds one arbitrary dirty scalar role for a fixed order-seven pair. PR #1495 covers three-register GL3 order-two swaps, and PR #1496 covers two-register GL3 order-four targets. The 2026-10-14 08:22 UTC REST overlap census covered all 419 open PR records; the latest complete cached Discussion snapshot had 371 records and no exact-scope match. Live Discussion refresh and posting were unavailable under the authenticated API rate limit; the local claim is in `CLAIM.md`.
